**STEP 1 - Scene:** This is a single piece of cooked sweet corn on the cob, cut crosswise into a short cylinder. It is photographed from directly above, so the cut end-face is visible. It sits alone on a white square plate.

**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The square plate has a diagonal of roughly 430 px, which I size at about 26-28 cm corner to corner, so the plate is about 20 cm across its sides. Its area is roughly 400-450 cm². The corn piece is about 100 px across, or about 6 cm in diameter.

**STEP 3 - Items:** One item is corn on the cob (cooked sweet corn, cob segment). There is no visible oil, butter, or sauce.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The corn's end-face covers about 30 cm² (π × 3 cm²), roughly 6-7% of the plate.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** About 30 cm² × 3.5 cm height ≈ 105 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Cob pieces with kernels are less dense than a solid mass because of the cob core and gaps. Using a bulk density of about 0.7 g/ml gives 105 × 0.7 ≈ 70 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Cooked sweet corn is about 96 kcal per 100 g. So 70 g × 0.96 ≈ 67 kcal. The woody cob core is inedible, so this figure is probably an upper bound.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** A single short corn-on-the-cob segment of about 70 g and roughly 65 kcal is plausible for what is visible. It is far smaller than a full plated meal, which matches the small amount of food on a large plate.
